title: The Bosphorus Brief: Regional Tensions Rise, Türkiye Steadies Course
overview: A tense day regionally, with the US-Iran strike-and-retaliation cycle dominating international coverage and a maritime incident off Istanbul adding local concern. For residents, the practical news is steadier: visa and economic developments continue quietly, and Türkiye's own posture toward its neighbors remains one of managed diplomacy rather than escalation.

sections.heading: Iran-US Escalation: What It Means Here
sections.body: Iran says a US strike on a wedding celebration in the south of the country killed at least four people, including children, and Tehran has called it a war crime; Washington denies targeting civilians. Iran responded with missile and drone strikes on US targets in the Middle East, and Ukrinform reports another Iranian ballistic missile was shot down over Turkish airspace — the second such interception noted recently. Saudi Arabia also says Iran struck a vessel in the Hormuz Strait, killing two sailors. None of this is occurring on Turkish soil, but the missile interceptions over Türkiye are a reminder that regional spillover is a live, if currently contained, risk. US travel advisories remain unchanged: Iran, Iraq, Syria, and Lebanon at Level 4; Türkiye at Level 2.

sections.heading: Maritime Incident Off Istanbul
sections.body: Turkish authorities have launched a search for a cargo ship after a vessel collision off Istanbul's coast, covered by Al Jazeera, DW, and Daily Sabah. Details on casualties or cause are still emerging; residents near the Bosphorus shipping lanes should watch for official updates rather than early reports.

sections.heading: Visas and Residency: Incremental Moves
sections.body: Türkiye has introduced visa-free travel for Syrian diplomats, part of a broader normalization in ties, according to Qazinform, Daily Sabah, and Kurdistan24. Separately, Türkiye's Tech Visa Program has drawn 47 startups to set up operations in the country, per Hürriyet Daily News and Anadolu Ajansı — a modest but concrete sign of continued interest from the tech sector despite economic headwinds. On the harder edge of the visa picture, musician Saint Levant has postponed a North American tour citing visa issues, and the Jerusalem Post reports Turkish authorities have been systematically identifying and targeting former IDF soldiers — a story that international and Israeli press are covering, but that has not appeared in Turkish state-aligned outlets.

sections.heading: Money: GDP Slows, Bonds Wobble Globally
sections.body: ING's analysis shows Turkey's second-quarter GDP growth was restrained by softer domestic demand, consistent with the broader tightening picture. Globally, a bond selloff is deepening on inflation and oil price pressures, raising borrowing costs for governments generally. The lira sits at 48.28 to the dollar and 55.98 to the euro today — worth noting for anyone timing transfers or major purchases this month.

closing: Stay alert to official channels on the Istanbul maritime search, and safe travels to those cheering on the volleyball team against Germany tonight.
